column1: # Pfam-A annotation benchmark (dev/perf/ab.sh and series.py with --file annot.tsv).
# All of Pfam-A 37.0 (21,979 models, --cut_ga) against six sets of 1,000 UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot
# proteins: bacteria, phage, fungi, viruses of eukaryotes, eukaryotes other than human, and
# human. Each set is split by length into four groups of 250 (L1 shortest .. L4 longest; the
# bounds are the set's own quartiles). The sets are defined in dev/bench/uniprot/sets.tsv and
# made by `dev/bench/uniprot.py fetch`.
#   U/  the UniProt sets (~/.cache/hmmer-bench/uniprot-*)    D/, F/, $NCPU: as in workloads.tsv
# Two forms of the same run: Pfam-A pressed with hmmpress (F/Pfam-A.hmm.h3m; hmmsearch also
# picks the pressed file up by itself when it sits next to Pfam-A.hmm) and the text file as
# downloaded (D/Pfam-A.hmm, workloads ending in _txt). --cut_ga thresholds are bit scores, so the
# threaded runs need no -Z to be deterministic.
@fixture Pfam-A.hmm.h3m  ln -sf D/Pfam-A.hmm Pfam-A.hmm && hmmpress Pfam-A.hmm > /dev/null
# ---- annot: pressed Pfam-A, $NCPU threads
